content: Melvin-Koushki concludes that Ibn Turka's conceptualization of lettrism is unique by the standards of the early ninth/fifteenth century: he inverts the relative importance of the pieces, so that theoretical lettrism, though neglected, is superior to letter magic, and neither Sufism nor philosophy contains or gives rise to lettrism but, as distinct, non-universal sciences, is itself encompassed by it.
